summary: Forest-edged water, small shrines, almost no one. The sacred pond near Subir tied to the Shabari story.
description:
A modest pond at the forest edge near Subir, which Dang's tradition identifies with the Pampa of the Ramayana, on whose banks Shabari's hermitage stood. Pilgrims bathe here before darshan at the main temple a few kilometres away, and it completes the Shabari Dham pair. Small shrines and ghats mark the waterline; the setting, still water, big trees, birdsong, does the rest.

As an experience it is the opposite of a headline sight: ten unhurried minutes for most visitors, longer for pilgrims and anyone happy to sit where it is quiet. Water levels and freshness are best from monsoon through winter. Combine it with Shabari Dham as one stop; alone it is a detour only devotees will rate.
highlights: The Pampa of Dang's Ramayana geography
history_legend: Regional tradition places Shabari's hermitage on Pampa's banks, where she waited a lifetime for Ram. Dang's identification of this pond as that Pampa rose to prominence alongside Shabari Dham in the 2000s, devotional geography, held with real local feeling.

modes.road: Signed village road off the Subir–Shabari Dham route
modes.rail: No practical railhead; district access via Waghai/Bilimora

access.last_mile: Short walk from parking to the ghats
access.road_condition: Narrow village tar; fine in all seasons

visit.notes: Open site; busiest during Ram Navami season alongside Shabari Dham.

seasonality.notes: Fullest and freshest monsoon through winter; shrinks and dulls by late summer.

experience.photography_notes: Still-water reflections early morning; egrets and kingfishers work the edges.

amenities.food: None on site; stalls at Shabari Dham and Subir

warnings: Bathe only at the ghat steps: the pond bed drops off unevenly

emergency.nearest_hospital: PHC Subir; Civil Hospital Ahwa (~28 km)

tips: Do it as the quiet second half of the Shabari Dham stop
Early morning is the site at its best, light, birds, stillness
